subject: Cold spin spike affecting p99 - customer escalation (FinTech Co.)
body:
From: Claire Park <cpark@fintechco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Increased p99 latency this morning — urgent

Mina,

We started seeing a sharp p99 latency increase on your Hosted API at ~07:50 PDT this morning. Error rates are low, but tail latency has spiked from ~420ms to >2.8s for a subset of requests during autoscale events. This correlates with three scale-outs we saw on our side. This is impacting two customer-facing flows (payment authorization & statement generation).

Attached: one sample request payload, a p99 trace, and basic request timestamps. Can you confirm if this is a known regression and whether you can mitigate? We need an estimated ETA for a fix or a temporary mitigation (e.g., disabling aggressive autoscale or warming strategy).

— Claire
Claire Park
SRE Lead, FinTech Co.
ops@fintechco.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <cpark@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 08:22:31 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased p99 latency this morning — urgent

Claire — thanks for the heads up. I’m escalating to infra and engineering now and will loop in ops if we need to coordinate config changes. Are the traces showing cold-start timing within the first 1-3 requests to a newly provisioned GPU? Any pattern on model or route?

I’ve copied Aditya (runtime), Hannah (CS lead), and Dylan (infra) and attached the logs you included.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Claire Park <cpark@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 08:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased p99 latency this morning — urgent

Claire / Mina,

We pulled the traces. Initial observation: during the autoscale events the new GPU instances are entering a "cold spin" where kernel compilation + KV-cache priming + model shard warm-up is sequential and causing a long tail for the first few requests. The p95 remains fine because most requests hit warmed workers, but p99 is dominated by those cold spin requests.

Evidence: trace shows a ~2.3s spend in kernel selection & jit path on cold instances and additional 200-400ms for weight page-in on the NVMe-backed local cache. We also see a small number of requests routed to a newly provisioned machine before the KV cache is populated.

Short-term mitigations we can apply immediately (config change + no code change):
- Temporarily set your route to prefer warm pool (if you have reserved/dedicated capacity) or reduce aggressive scale-up thresholds for the next 12–24h.
- Enable request throttling with queued warmup to avoid racing many first-requests at once.
- Add a shallow retry on the client side with jitter — fastest to adopt if you can.

Medium-term engineering follow-ups (we own):
- Implement a lightweight pre-warm ping that triggers kernel selection and KV priming before accepting production traffic.
- Change autoscaler placement policy to not schedule traffic on a node until KV cache snapshot is applied.
- Introduce a fast-start path for frequently used routes: cached kernels and preloaded quantized weights.

We’ll open an internal incident and post updates. Would you like us to apply the temporary config change for you?

— Aditya Rao
Principal Software Engineer, Runtime
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Claire Park <cpark@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Increased p99 latency this morning — urgent

We can flip a routing flag to prevent newly provisioned GPUs from taking production traffic until they report a "ready_for_traffic" healthcheck (includes KV primed). That’s low-risk and reversible. I propose: gate traffic until we've seen 2 successful warm pings or 30s since instance creation, whichever comes first.

If you want us to apply immediately, confirm and I’ll schedule the change against your route (we can do a short maintenance window). Note: this increases cold capacity ihtiyaç (will mention to your cost team) because nodes spend a few extra seconds warmed without traffic.

— Dylan Brooks
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Claire Park <cpark@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 11:03:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased p99 latency this morning — urgent

Claire — thank you for the sample traces and the quick context. We’ll coordinate with your SREs to roll the routing flag change now as a temporary mitigation. Mina, please confirm that FinTech Co. approves the short maintenance window (5–10 min) for the toggle. Claire — can we do the toggle at 12:00 PDT? We’ll monitor p99 for 30 minutes after and share dashboards.

Action items:
- FinTech Co.: confirm maintenance window 12:00 PDT (Claire)
- Redwood infra: prepare routing gate + healthcheck (Dylan)
- Runtime: instrument priming metrics and add a trace ID to the pre-warm pings (Aditya)
- CS: hold updates and expected ETA to FinTech Co. (Mina/Hannah)

— Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 12:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased p99 latency this morning — urgent

Claire — FinTech Co. confirmed — please proceed with the maintenance window at 12:00 PDT. We appreciate the quick triage. Please send the post-change dashboard snapshot to this thread.

Thanks all — Mina

-----Original Message-----
From: Claire Park <cpark@fintechco.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 14:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased p99 latency this morning — urgent

Team — we ran the toggle at 12:00 PDT. Initial results: p99 dropped from ~2.8s to ~470ms within 5 minutes and stabilized around 380–520ms over the 30-minute window. No functional regressions observed. We’ll continue monitoring for the next 24 hours and will share a fuller set of telemetry tomorrow.

Thank you for the fast response — Claire
